semantically_equivalent_models.justification: The term 'rnn models' is a general reference to various types of recurrent neural networks, including modular recurrent neural networks, hence they are semantically equivalent.

parent_models.justification: 'Modular recurrent neural network' is a type of recurrent neural network, making 'recurrent neural networks' a parent model.
All recurrent neural networks, including modular variants, are a subset of neural networks, making 'neural network' a parent model.
'RNNS' serve as an acronym for recurrent neural networks, thus encompassing modular recurrent neural networks as well.
This is a broader category that includes all types of neural network architectures, including modular recurrent neural networks.
A broad category that includes recurrent neural networks as well as other neural network forms.
A plural form that represents a broader category encompassing various neural networks including modular recurrent neural networks.

closest_parent_model.justification: 'Recurrent neural networks' specifically identifies the general class of neural networks to which 'modular recurrent neural networks' belong, making it the closest and most specific parent model.

child_models.justification: 'Simple recurrent neural networks' refer to a specific architecture within the realm of recurrent neural networks and can be considered under modular forms depending on the configuration.

closest_child_model.justification: This is the most basic form of a recurrent neural network, and while it may not explicitly include modular components, it is the simplest and closest specific adaptation under the broader category of recurrent neural networks.

sibling_models.justification: It is a variant within the broad category of recurrent neural networks that serve different, specific purposes and structures than modular RNNs.
Another specialized type of recurrent neural network that contrasts with modular recurrent neural networks in structure and functionality.
Represents a distinct approach within recurrent architecture focusing on interactions between sequences, analogous to modular adaptations in complexity.
This model applies recurrent network principles to perform inference tasks, distinct from modular RNNs yet within the sibling category.
A form of recurrent neural network with a probabilistic twist, categorized alongside modular structures as a sibling due to similar complexity.
An advanced application of recurrent network principles to reinforcement learning, which parallels modular RNNs in sophistication.

closest_sibling_model.justification: This model parallels modular RNNs due to its complexity and specific sequence interactions, aligning closely in addressing specific computational requirements compared to other sibling models.

unrelated_models.justification: Feed-forward networks represent a distinct, non-recurrent type of neural network architecture, unrelated to recurrent structures.
Generally refers to depth in layer count but is more associated with static architectures unlike recurrent structures.
A combination of layer depth and a feed-forward approach, differing fundamentally from recurrent networks.
They focus on direct, multi-layer processing without feedback loops characteristic of recurrent networks.
While it is a type of recurrent network, its specific characteristics differentiate it enough to not consider it directly under modular RNN concepts.
Explicitly a non-recurrent architecture, differentiating it from recurrent forms fundamentally.
A very broad term that, while inclusive, lacks the specificity needed to relate directly to modular RNNs when considering functional roles.
